titleEn: Hat On, Water Jug in Hand—Let's Go!

pages.text: "Let's go to the paddy!" Little pig Dingding, wearing an apron, hurried down the bank empty-handed. Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, asked from behind, "Have you got everything?" "Yes, I'm ready!" Dingding did not look back.
The sun blazed, and Dingding's head grew hot. "Oh, my hat!" Dingding climbed back up. From above, Dingding saw Mom setting down her jug one paddy level below.
Dingding came down wearing the hat. Now their throat was dry. "Oh, my water jug!" Mom was already two levels below. "Do I have to climb back up again?" Dingding pouted.
Mom came up the bank and sat in front of Dingding, looking into their eyes. "You only need to count two things before we go." She held up two fingers.

Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, brought down Dingding's jug. "You left this behind." Mom tapped the hat, then the jug. "These two will help you in the paddy." "Hat and water jug!" Dingding repeated.
"Starting tomorrow, let's count them at the doorway." Dingding took the jug and pulled the hat snugly on. Mom folded her fingers as she sang, "Hat On, Water Jug in Hand—Let's Go!"

The next morning, Dingding stood by the doorway hooks and counted while getting ready. "One, hat on! Two, water jug in hand!" The hat went on their head, the jug into their hand. "Hat On, Water Jug in Hand—Let's Go!"

Dingding went down the bank. There was a hat for the hot sun and water for a thirsty throat. Dingding sniffed the lovely spring paddy smell. "I didn't leave anything behind!" Dingding reached the paddy before Mom.
The following day, Dingding got ready at the doorway before Mom asked. "One, hat! Two, water jug! Three, let's go!" Dingding called, "Hat On, Water Jug in Hand—Let's Go!"

Mom lifted Dingding into a hug. "You can get everything ready yourself now!" Counting the two things at the doorway saved extra trips up and down the bank. Dingding pressed the hat down. "Hat On, Water Jug in Hand—Let's Go!"
